Weekly Discovery — Saturday, October 10 2026

Claude's eval-building workflow and Home Assistant's native MCP integration reshape local automation and AI integration

Claude Ecosystem

#1 — Claude API adds guided eval design and hillclimbing workflows in claude-api skill — Anthropic / Releasebot

★ New claude-api skill capability directly addresses your capability gap in systematic evaluation workflows for agent systems running on your canonical Git-native context repo.

Anthropic added guided build-eval and hillclimb workflows in the claude-api skill, helping users create evaluations, validate graders, and improve apps while checking for overfitting and noise. On held-out test cases, the final configuration scored 90.5% against the original setup's 78.6%, at about one fifth of the cost.

#2 — Claude Code mods enable deeper behavior customization for plugins and automations — Anthropic / Releasebot

★ Mods expand Claude Code's flexibility for your custom skill ecosystem and hook infrastructure; this is a breaking change in control flow that affects how to design future automation in .claude/skills.

Claude Mods gained deeper behavior customization on October 1, 2026; a built-in side agent can flag overlooked issues. Fixed skills and custom commands to refuse shell commands containing raw control characters, with a message showing where they are.

#3 — Home Assistant 2026.10 integrates native MCP server with one-click setup — Forkast / Home Assistant

★ This is the ecosystem bridge you need: Home Assistant now exposes 2,000+ integrations via MCP, making your existing smart home context available to Claude Code and Claude Desktop through a single protocol — a primitive your setup has been waiting for.

Home Assistant 2026.10, releasing October 7, integrates the Model Context Protocol (MCP) directly into the platform, allowing you to turn your entire home into a single, accessible context for any AI agent you choose to use. MCP exposes over 2,000 built-in integrations via a local /api/mcp endpoint with one-click setup so AI agents like Claude or ChatGPT can control Zigbee, Z‑Wave and Matter devices locally.

Home Automation

#1 — Home Assistant 2026.10: MCP integration, OpenStreetMap vector map, and improved automations — Smart Home Assistant / Home Assistant

★ Material update affecting your running setup: breaking changes you must review before update (legacy auth removal, MQTT publish admin-only), plus the MCP server capability that makes your 2,000+ integrations agent-accessible without subscription.

Home Assistant 2026.10, officially releasing October 7 at 4:00 PM ET, integrates the Model Context Protocol (MCP) directly into the platform. Breaking changes include legacy authentication removal, SolarEdge Local removal and admin-only MQTT publish and dump actions. The release brings an improved automation editor where you can add a "Triggered by" condition and tick the ones that you want, making paired automations simpler.

#2 — Philips Hue firmware 1.164.2 adds Zigbee and Matter concurrency on newer bulbs — Local Smart Home Guide

★ Concrete firmware improvement for a device class in your stack (mains-powered smart lights); if you own newer Hue Thread bulbs, this firmware enables them to strengthen your Thread mesh without leaving the Bridge—direct capability upgrade.

Philips Hue released lamp firmware 1.164.2 on October 5 for lights on hardware platform 100b-129, with Matter 1.4.1 support and "Zigbee and Matter concurrency in bridgeless mode." The platform covers all 2026 Hue products plus E27 bulbs and GU10 spots from fall 2025, the ones with Thread radios, and a light first set up over Thread can later be added to a Hue Bridge without re-pairing.

#3 — Matter 1.6 released June 2026 — focus on setup, multi-ecosystem management, and thermostat behavior — Data Wire Solutions

★ Specification update affecting your Matter integration strategy; 1.6 adds thermostat behavior and multi-ecosystem management, both relevant to your Netatmo TRVs and Airzone dual-system HVAC architecture.

Matter 1.6, released June 17, 2026, is the latest Matter specification and does not add new device categories; it focuses on setup, multi-ecosystem management, thermostat behavior, status reporting, and security infrastructure. Home Assistant has full Matter and Thread integration, requiring a dedicated Thread radio (sold separately as the Home Assistant SkyConnect/ZBT-1 dongle) and is best for privacy-first, local-control users.
